after.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $B=PD{P}^{-1},$ find $\operatorname{ln}⁡B.$
after.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and the given matrix $B,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡B=\operatorname{ln}⁡(PD{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $D$ is a diagonal matrix, we get

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡D=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡1 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2\cdot 1-1\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡B & =P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Computing the Value of a Function of a Jordan Decomposition
content.problem:
Consider the following matrices:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}],\,D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}],\,P=[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $B=PD{P}^{-1},$ find $\operatorname{ln}⁡B.$
content.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)=\operatorname{ln}⁡x$ and the given matrix $B,$ we have

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡B=\operatorname{ln}⁡(PD{P}^{-1})=P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $D$ is a diagonal matrix, we get

$$
\operatorname{ln}⁡D=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡1 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{2\cdot 1-1\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡B & =P\cdot (\operatorname{ln}⁡D)\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2 \\ -\operatorname{ln}⁡2 & 2\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.worked_solution:
Given a function $f$ and matrices $A$ and $S,$ where $S$ is invertible, we have

$$
f(SA{S}^{-1})=S\cdot f(A)\cdot {S}^{-1}.
$$

For $f(x)={2}^{x}$ and the given matrix $A,$ we have

$$
{2}^{A}={2}^{(PD{P}^{-1})}=P\cdot ({2}^{D})\cdot {P}^{-1}.
$$

Now, since $D$ is a diagonal matrix, we get

$$
{2}^{D}=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & {2}^{3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].
$$

Also, the inverse of $P$ is

$$
{P}^{-1}=\frac{1}{1\cdot 1-0\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{2}^{A} & =P\cdot ({2}^{D})\cdot {P}^{-1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 4 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 \\ 0 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
f({J}_{n}(\lambda ))=[\begin{aligned}f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & \frac{{f}^{″}(\lambda )}{2!} & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-1)}(\lambda )}{(n-1)!} \\ 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) & ⋯ & \frac{{f}^{(n-2)}(\lambda )}{(n-2)!} \\ ⋮ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋱ & ⋮ \\ 0 & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda ) & {f}^{′}(\lambda ) \\ 0 & ⋯ & ⋯ & 0 & f(\lambda )\end{aligned}].
$$

First, note that

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3})\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(\frac{\pi }{4})) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡([\begin{aligned}{J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & 0 \\ 0 & {J}_{1}(\pi )\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3})) & 0 \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡({J}_{1}(\pi ))\end{aligned}] \\  & =\operatorname{cos}⁡({J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3}))\,⊕\,\operatorname{cos}⁡({J}_{1}(\pi )).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we compute the function of each Jordan block separately.

- For ${J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3}),$ we have $n=3$ and $\lambda =2.$ \since $n=3,$ we need to compute the first and second derivatives of $f$ only:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

So, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{3}(\frac{\pi }{3})) & =[\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{3}) & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) & \frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\ 0 & f(\frac{\pi }{3}) & {f}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & f(\frac{\pi }{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) & -\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\ 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3}) \\ 0 & 0 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{3})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}f({J}_{1}(\pi )) & =[\begin{aligned}f(\pi )\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
